children: received an Overweight rating due in part to strong data center demand and supportive merger and acquisition activity as Morgan Stanley initiated coverage.
Shares of SiTime surged 9% during early Thursday market action.

"SiTime operates as a pure-play in the precision timing portion of the market, where greater accuracy and stability are required for more demanding applications," said Morgan Stanley analyst Joseph Moore in a Thursday investor report. "Its SAM has expanded from ~$1bn in 2020 to ~$4bn today, with further runway from MEMS adoption replacing quartz, continued share gains and TPD cross-sell. We model 30% total/31% organic revenue growth in CY28, above management's 25-30% long-term framework."
Morgan Stanley set a $730 price target on the stock, noting that last week's 13% drop during a broad semiconductor sell-off has created an entry point.

"SiTime's AI/data center exposure reached 64% of revenue in the most recent quarter, up from 12% at IPO, spanning both networking and compute," Moore added. "We expect optical to remain the clearest near-term driver as 1.6T ramps, while inference workloads broaden the compute opportunity and add timing content, supporting our 38% CY28 growth forecast."
Regarding acquisitions, SiTime completed its purchase of certain assets from Renesas Electronics

"The acquisition of Renesas' timing business marks a monumental milestone that will transform SiTime," said SiTime CEO Rajesh Vashist. "We are accelerating our path to $1B in revenue, growing our clocking portfolio by 10x, expanding our presence in the high-growth AI datacenter market and scaling our gross margins to the higher end of our target range."
